quantities: E[X_{tau_c-}] given tau_c < infinity, from one type-1 founder
E[Y_{tau_c-}] given tau_c < infinity, from one type-1 founder
adjustment_reason: birth and death held equal across both types and fixed throughout, with birth above death, so that nu is the only demographic parameter varying between columns; nu = 0.4 = lambda - mu is exactly the type-1 criticality point
parameter_note: these demographic rates differ deliberately both from fig_bio_regimes (lambda1=1.0, mu1=0.45, nu=0.35, lambda2=0.85, mu2=0.40) and from the worked example in section 10 of the teaching document; the three are not one parameter family

domain_note.delta1_zero: regular; catastrophe remains reachable through the type-2 channel, so the delta1 = 0 edge is retained
domain_note.delta2_zero: singular and therefore excluded. On delta2 = 0 one has G == 1, hence theta2 = lambda2 - mu2 > 0, and E[Y_{tau-}] diverges whenever theta1(inf) + (lambda2 - mu2) > 0. At delta1 = 0 the discriminant is a perfect square and the criterion collapses to |lambda1 - mu1 - nu| < lambda2 - mu2
domain_note.threshold_meaning: largest delta1 for which the delta2 = 0 edge is still divergent; 0.0 means that edge is regular for every delta1 >= 0

horizon_selfcheck.method: fraction of each running integral accumulated in the final 5 percent of [0,T]

step_halving.method: max absolute change in E[X], E[Y] when RK4 steps are doubled, over a spread of points including the small-delta corner

flux_identity.statement: J_1(1,1,t) = delta1*m_x + delta2*m_y must equal -S'(t); J_2(1,1,t) = delta2*n_y must equal -G'(t)

gillespie.method: exact continuous-time simulation, 120000 paths per point, recording (X,Y) in the instant before catastrophe
gillespie.result: all within about two standard errors

open_observation.statement: at nu = lambda - mu = 0.4 with delta1 = delta2 = delta, the computed E[Y_{tau-}] equals (lambda - mu)/delta to all printed digits (4.0000 at delta=0.10, 1.6000 at delta=0.25). It does not hold at other nu, nor when delta1 != delta2.
open_observation.status: numerical observation only; not derived. Recorded as a remark and an open exercise in teaching_precatastrophe.tex section 11; not claimed in main.tex

used_by: teaching_precatastrophe.tex, section 11 (The parameter plane); not used by main.tex
